Subject: Post-demo recap + procurement path questions

Hi Linda — great speaking earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so the procurement team has the right options laid out: 

- Summary: FluxGrid is interested in Redwood for low-latency inference across ML features in the customer portal. Primary concerns: predictable monthly spend, SSO + audit logs, and procurement process constraints.
- Commercial paths we discussed: card on file (self-serve), purchase order (PO) with monthly invoice, or procurement via AWS Marketplace (license through marketplace SaaS contract).
- Procurement ask: can you confirm whether FluxGrid prefers (choose one) — a) PO + standard 30-day invoice; b) charge card; or c) Marketplace purchase (AWS or GCP) to simplify billing? Also: do you require a vendor W9 + SOW or is a standard SOW + PO sufficient?

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_template_v1.pdf (SOW template), SOC2_summary.pdf (security snapshot).

Proposed next steps:
1) If PO preferred — please share procurement contact + any PO template + billing address.
2) If Marketplace — confirm which marketplace (AWS / GCP / Azure) and whether you need a private offer. If AWS, we can provide a marketplace listing ID and quote path; private offers are supported.
3) If card — we’ll send an activation link and standard T&Cs.

I’ll follow up with a short mutual action plan after you confirm the route. Looping in Marissa (AE) for commercial and Laura (legal) for any contract redlines.

Thanks,

Procurement team — thanks for the note, and copying Laura and Vivek for legal/solutions details. Answering the procurement questions and outlining concrete options so you can pick the simplest path: 

Option A — PO + monthly invoices (our standard enterprise flow)
- Process: we execute Master Services Agreement (MSA) + SOW; you issue PO referencing the SOW; Redwood invoices monthly net-30.
- Docs needed: PO, billing address, W9 (we can provide), signed SOW.
- Timeline: ~2–5 business days after signed SOW and PO for provisioning on Dedicated or Hosted.

Option B — Card on file (fastest to pilot)
- Process: FluxGrid signs up, card is charged monthly; standard commercial T&Cs applied via checkout.
- Pros: <24h activation for hosted; minimal paperwork.

Option C — AWS Marketplace (recommended if you want centralized cloud billing)
- Process variants: 1) Buy public listing (standard); 2) Private Offer (vendor issues private offer through AWS marketplace with negotiated price/term).
- From Redwood side: we can create a private offer that maps to the same SOW/commercial terms; AWS will still handle billing to FluxGrid and remit to Redwood.
- Docs needed: Marketplace quote ID for purchase + (optional) SOW for term details.
- Note: Marketplace purchases sometimes require AWS Marketplace seller verification and additional lead time for private offers (~3–7 business days).

Key questions for procurement to confirm:
1) Do you need Redwood to produce a private offer on AWS (yes/no)? If yes, who is the billing owner (AWS account ID)?
2) Billing address and full PO template.
3) Any special tax or remittance instructions.

Next steps I’ll take:
- Marissa will prepare a short mutual action plan with estimated pricing tiers for PO vs Marketplace.
- Laura will prepare a minimal MSA + SOW copy for procurement review (attached SOW template).
- Vivek will draft the technical acceptance checklist for onboarding on Dedicated vs Hosted.

If procurement confirms AWS private offer is desired, I'll initiate the private offer workflow and share the AWS Marketplace listing ID and draft quote.

Thanks,
Sergio
